question: What is the primary goal of palliative care?

options.A: Speeding up the natural dying process for terminal patients
options.B: Improving the quality of life for patients and their families
options.C: Curing underlying chronic pathologies through aggressive therapy
options.D: Providing long-term institutionalized care for the elderly

explanation: Palliative care focuses primarily on enhancing the quality of daily life and alleviating suffering rather than attempting to reverse or cure the disease process. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: When is the most appropriate time to introduce palliative care into a patient's treatment plan?

options.A: Immediately upon diagnosing any acute, self-limiting infectious disease
options.B: Exclusively during the final twenty-four hours of active dying
options.C: Only after all curative and disease-modifying options have completely failed
options.D: Early in the course of a life-threatening illness alongside curative treatments

explanation: Integrating palliative care early helps manage symptoms effectively throughout the entire trajectory of a serious illness, rather than waiting until the end of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: How does palliative care view the process of dying?

options.A: As a normal and natural process
options.B: As a pathological state requiring urgent reversal
options.C: As an entirely preventable medical complication
options.D: As an administrative failure of modern medicine

explanation: Palliative care philosophy accepts dying as a natural part of the human life cycle, aiming neither to artificially hasten nor postpone death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which principle is central to the palliative care philosophy regarding the patient and family unit?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on physiological laboratory markers
options.B: Transferring all decision-making duties to the attending physician
options.C: Treating the patient and family as a combined unit of care
options.D: Isolating the patient to prevent emotional burden on relatives

explanation: Because serious illness impacts everyone close to the patient, palliative care extends its support and assessment to the entire family network. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: What distinguishes palliative care from purely curative treatment?

options.A: Curative treatment ignores physical symptoms entirely in favor of lab values
options.B: Curative treatment is restricted exclusively to pediatric populations
options.C: Palliative care prioritizes comfort and quality of life over disease eradication
options.D: Palliative care can only be delivered inside specialized hospice facilities

explanation: While curative care aims to remove the disease, palliative care centers on relieving suffering and supporting well-being regardless of disease status. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is true regarding the timeline of palliative care versus curative care?

options.A: Palliative care must finish before curative treatment can begin
options.B: Curative treatment is only started after palliative care fails
options.C: They can be administered simultaneously throughout an illness
options.D: They share identical clinical objectives and protocols

explanation: Patients frequently receive disease-modifying or curative treatments at the same time they receive supportive palliative symptom management. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h3)

question: Who typically acts as the central communication hub and coordinator of daily care within the multidisciplinary team?
explanation: Nurses spend the most continuous time with patients, placing them in an ideal position to coordinate care across various disciplines and monitor symptom changes. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary approach necessary in palliative care?

options.A: Specialized teams reduce the total cost of hospital infrastructure
options.B: Physicians are legally prohibited from speaking with family members alone
options.C: Hospital accreditation boards mandate a minimum of ten staff per room
options.D: Total suffering encompasses physical, emotional, social, and spiritual dimensions

explanation: Because end-of-life and chronic illness challenges affect multiple facets of human existence, diverse professionals are needed to address every dimension of care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: What does the term 'total pain' encompass in palliative care?

options.A: Physical nociceptive pain that is completely resistant to opioids
options.B: Neuropathic pain localized strictly to the lower extremities
options.C: Physical, psychological, social, and spiritual components of suffering
options.D: Only the maximum score recorded on a numerical rating scale

explanation: Total pain acknowledges that physical discomfort is intensely magnified by emotional, social, and spiritual distress. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: A patient with advanced cancer experiences severe, constant pain that is no longer controlled by non-opioid medications. According to the WHO analgesic ladder, what is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Discontinuing all analgesics to prevent drug tolerance
options.B: Relying solely on relaxation therapy and distraction
options.C: Progressing to a weak or strong opioid analgesic
options.D: Increasing the dosage of non-opioids beyond safe limits

explanation: When baseline non-opioids fail to control pain, stepping up to appropriate opioid therapy is the standard evidence-based management strategy. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: How should a nurse handle traditional or cultural practices requested by a patient and family during end-of-life care?

options.A: Ignore them completely as they have no bearing on health outcomes
options.B: Integrate and respect them safely within the care plan whenever possible
options.C: Report the family to hospital security for violating facility policy
options.D: Prohibit them immediately to maintain strict hospital sterile routines

explanation: Respecting cultural and spiritual traditions provides immense comfort and emotional security to patients and their families during vulnerable times. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is a primary goal of addressing spiritual needs in palliative care?

options.A: Converting the patient to a specific religious doctrine
options.B: Complying with mandatory federal theological testing
options.C: Helping the patient find meaning, peace, and hope
options.D: Replacing the need for physical pain medication

explanation: Spiritual care focuses on existential well-being, helping individuals find inner peace, resolve conflicts, and derive meaning from their life experience. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which clinical sign is commonly observed during the active dying phase?

options.A: Significant weight gain from systemic fluid retention
options.B: Sudden spikes in systolic blood pressure and hyperactivity
options.C: Altered breathing patterns such as Cheyne-Stokes respirations
options.D: Increased visual acuity and alertness right before death

explanation: Irregular breathing patterns, periods of apnea, and noisy respiratory secretions are hallmark physiological signs of approaching death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h7)

question: When does comprehensive bereavement support for a grieving family ideally begin?

options.A: Six months following the formal issuance of the death certificate
options.B: Before the patient's death through anticipatory guidance
options.C: Exclusively when requested by legal representatives in court
options.D: Only after the funeral rites and burial have concluded

explanation: Support begins early by preparing families for impending changes, helping them process anticipatory grief before the actual loss occurs. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is a major systemic challenge nurses often face when delivering palliative care in many Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: An overabundance of specialized palliative physicians on every ward
options.B: Excessive funding that complicates financial record keeping
options.C: Restricted access to essential pain medications like oral morphine
options.D: Mandatory laws forbidding nurses from touching patients in pain

explanation: Regulatory hurdles and supply chain limitations often restrict the availability of strong opioids, making pain management a distinct clinical challenge in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which action best demonstrates the nurse acting as a patient advocate in palliative settings?

options.A: Withholding information about diagnosis to prevent emotional upset
options.B: Encouraging relatives to limit visiting hours to reduce noise
options.C: Following physician orders blindly without checking for patient comfort
options.D: Ensuring the patient's expressed wishes and pain relief needs are communicated to the medical team

explanation: Advocacy involves standing up for the patient's rights, preferences, and comfort levels when interacting with the broader multidisciplinary healthcare team. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h8)
